title: CoinRun final-policy dynamics fixed-20k scale sweep
question: At fixed 16.6M tokenizer, final-policy trajectory data, optimizer updates and held-out futures, how does CoinRun dynamics rollout quality change from 0.16M to 12.90M parameters?
reason: The previous capacity sweep used a 0.17M tokenizer, random-action data and the wrong 16-action/no-op contract. Scale must be re-measured after fixing representation, action semantics and trajectory quality.
hypothesis: With the corrected 15-action/no-op-4 contract and final-policy data, held-out mean-frame PSNR and SSIM improve from tiny to small to medium; the large model should at least match medium when every scale receives 20,000 optimizer updates.
falsification: Reject the monotonic scale hypothesis if small does not exceed tiny, medium does not exceed small, or large falls below medium on either mean-frame PSNR or mean SSIM under the fixed evaluation set.

source.source_freeze: Execution code is frozen at d8d7a925d7ff57423f9591551581cb4c39e08bc7. No scale-sweep result was observed before the freeze.

data.provenance: The train and evaluation corpora are produced and audited by CR-DYN-0006 before this sweep starts.

compute.estimated_budget: Tiny, small and large 20k arms run after CR-DYN-0006; the exact medium final-policy arm is reused, for approximately 8-14 additional A10-hours.
compute.shutdown_policy: One existing A10 only, serial arms, no concurrent training; preserve an OOM as a failed arm rather than silently changing batch or architecture.

training.medium_reuse: Reuse the byte-identical ppo25p17m-medium arm from CR-DYN-0006 instead of spending a second identical run.

success_criteria.rule: The four scale points use the same final-policy train corpus, 16.6M EMA tokenizer, batch size, 20,000 updates, optimizer recipe and fixed held-out futures.
Every non-reused arm starts from scratch and reaches the exact final checkpoint step 19,999; an OOM or instability remains a failed arm.
Support monotonic scaling only if tiny < small < medium <= large for both mean-frame PSNR and mean SSIM.
